claims.text: The integrated combination of electromagnetic levitation, ultrahigh-speed DSC, in situ synchrotron XRD, and CALPHAD calibration can accurately measure melting temperatures in high-entropy alloys.
The integrated system can accurately measure enthalpy and entropy of fusion in high-entropy alloys.
The integrated system can accurately determine volume changes at melting in high-entropy alloys.
The integrated system can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across a wide range of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed integrated system will be efficient for high-throughput characterization across diverse alloy compositions.
Melting temperatures can be measured with errors below 2% relative to benchmark systems.
Fusion enthalpies can be measured within 5% of established values or predictions.
Fusion entropies can be measured within 5% of established values or predictions.
Maintaining samples under ultra-high vacuum or inert gas avoids contamination.
Real-time synchrotron XRD can track atomic-scale structural changes during rapid phase transitions.
Concurrent XRD patterns can associate latent-heat peaks detected by DSC with the occurrence of melting.
Containerless processing eliminates contamination from sample containers.
Containerless processing eliminates or suppresses heterogeneous nucleation issues.
Reducing contamination and heterogeneous nucleation allows DSC to capture latent heat and transient thermodynamic signals accurately.
CALPHAD provides a computational baseline that can translate the combined calorimetric and structural observations into comprehensive thermodynamic properties.
Synchrotron XRD can provide reliable volume-change measurements during melting.
Traditional stand-alone DSC or XRD methods lack the integrated temporal resolution needed to capture rapid transient phenomena in high-entropy alloys.
The lack of integrated temporal resolution in traditional methods results in less accurate thermodynamic-property measurements.
The approach is expected to be most effective for milligram-scale samples under rapid heating or cooling in high-purity controlled environments.
The individual measurement techniques have previously demonstrated high accuracy.
